Gil Strang defines the Gibonacci numbers $G_n$ as follows. We begin with $G_0 = 0$ and $G_1=1$. A subsequent Gibonacci number is the average of the two previous; that is, $G_{n+2} = \frac12(G_{n}+G_{n+1})$. We then have $$ \begin{aligned} G_{n+2} \amp {}={} \frac12 G_{n} + \frac 12 G_{n+1} \\ G_{n+1} \amp {}={} G_{n+1}\text{.} \\ \end{aligned} $$

If $\xvec_n=\twovec{G_{n+1}}{G_n}$, find the matrix $A$ such that $\xvec_{n+1} = A\xvec_n$.

Find the eigenvalues and associated eigenvectors of $A$.

Explain why this dynamical system does not neatly fit into one of the six types that we saw in this section.

Write $\xvec_{0}$ as a linear combination of eigenvectors of $A$.

Write $\xvec_n$ as a linear combination of eigenvectors of $A$.

What happens to $G_n$ as $n$ becomes very large?
